title: One-Pot Tomato & Spinach Cheese Tortellini
description: Refrigerated cheese tortellini simmers in a simple tomato broth with spinach for a fast one-pot dinner.
substitutions: Use frozen cheese tortellini and add a few minutes to the cooking time.
Use chopped kale instead of spinach and add it with the tomatoes.
Skip the cheese topping for a lighter bowl.

steps.text: Simmer the tomato broth and tortellini.

cookSteps.text: Combine 1 can diced tomatoes, 2 cups broth, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Add 1 package cheese tortellini, reduce to a steady simmer, cover, and cook according to the package timing until tender, usually 7–10 minutes.
Stir in 2 cups baby spinach and cook 1–2 minutes, until wilted.
Divide into bowls and top with up to 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella or Parmesan if using.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. The tortellini will absorb broth, so add a splash of water or broth when reheating.

title: Ham, Cheddar & Broccoli Egg Scramble
description: Eggs, deli or leftover ham, broccoli, and cheddar make a quick skillet meal for breakfast or dinner.

ingredients.item: diced cooked ham or chopped deli ham

substitutions: Use frozen broccoli, thawed and patted dry.
Use cooked sausage instead of ham.
Use Monterey Jack or another easy-melting cheese instead of cheddar.

steps.text: Soften the broccoli and warm the ham.
Scramble in the eggs and cheese.

cookSteps.text: Melt 1 tablespoon butter or heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add 1 cup finely chopped broccoli and cook 3 minutes.
Add 3/4 cup diced ham and cook 2 minutes, until hot.
Beat 4 eggs with 2 tablespoons milk if using. Pour into the skillet and cook, stirring gently, for 3–4 minutes until softly set.
Sprinkle in 1/2 cup shredded cheddar, fold once or twice until melted, and serve.

storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days and reheat gently until hot.

title: Leftover Chicken, Rice & Corn Soup
description: Cooked chicken and rice become a fast comforting soup with corn and ordinary pantry broth.
substitutions: Use cooked turkey instead of chicken.
Use cooked noodles instead of rice.
Add leftover cooked carrots, peas, or broccoli if you have them.

steps.text: Add leftovers and simmer until hot.

cookSteps.text: Combine 5 cups chicken broth, 1 1/2 cups corn, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper in a large saucepan. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in 2 cups cooked chicken and 2 cups cooked rice. Simmer 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until everything is steaming hot.
Taste and season if needed, then serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Rice thickens the soup as it sits; add broth or water when reheating.

title: Small-Batch Chocolate Peanut Butter Rice Crisps
description: Crispy rice cereal, peanut butter, and chocolate make a tiny no-bake batch when you want something sweet without turning on the oven.
substitutions: Use another plain crisp rice-style cereal.
Use maple syrup instead of honey; the bars may be slightly softer.
Use milk chocolate chips instead of semisweet.

steps.text: Coat the cereal with warm peanut butter mixture.
Press, top with chocolate, and chill.

cookSteps.text: Put 2 1/2 cups crispy rice cereal in a mixing bowl. Line or lightly grease a small dish or loaf pan.
Warm 1/2 cup peanut butter and 1/4 cup honey or corn syrup in a small saucepan over low heat for 2–3 minutes, stirring until smooth. Do not boil.
Pour over the cereal and stir until coated. Press firmly into the prepared dish.
Melt 1/2 cup chocolate chips with 1 teaspoon butter if using in short microwave bursts or over very low heat. Spread over the cereal layer.
Chill about 30 minutes until firm, then cut into 6 pieces.

storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 2 days or refrigerate up to 1 week.
